To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) intrinsic motivation is the most important type of self-determined regulation in the workplace, and that (2) identified regulation is the next most important type of regulation.
intrinsic motivation and identified motivation are differentially related to the motivating potential of the work, autonomy support from supervisors, and understanding of strategy.

the job’s motivating characteristics (i.e. autonomy, feedback, task identity, task significance, task variety, and skill variety) as well as the leadership style (i.e. the extent to which supervisors support employees’ autonomy) and the extent to which employees understand their organization’s strategy are associated with job satisfaction, turnover intentions, and organizational citizenship behaviors (i.e. civic virtue and altruistic behaviors) through intrinsic and identified motivation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether and how the job design, the leadership style, and strategy of the organization influence employee motivation and behavior.
the question of how the job’s motivating-potential, the leadership style, and the strategy of the organization influence employee outcomes.
the impact of work design, autonomy support, and strategy on employee motivation and behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the motivational processes are not only relevant but also different.
intrinsic motivation and identified extrinsic motivation are important mediators between antecedents and outcomes.
the more self-determined a motivation is, the stronger is the association between antecedents and outcomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
self-determined motivation is not only important to predict employee behavior but also to predict the impact of contextual factors on employee behavior.
the motivational processes of intrinsic motivation and identified extrinsic regulation are more important for the explanation of employee outcomes than controlled types of behavioral regulations.
the more employees are intrinsically motivated, the more they will be satisfied with their job and the more they will engage in OCB.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the motivational processes of self-determination theory are not equally relevant to explain all work outcomes, and that the motivational process of intrinsic motivation is particularly relevant to explain the relationship between contextual antecedents and OCB.
the impact of contextual work design factors on OCB is mediated by intrinsic motivation and identified motivation.
the impact of contextual factors on employee outcomes is mediated through different types of self-determination at the job level.
